property_summary: For any owner-triggered call to sudicideAnyone and any initial balance, C destroys itself and sends all its ether away, leaving address(c).balance == 0; the mutant never selfdestructs, so its balance stays nonzero for some amount.

After funding c with any amount and the owner calling sudicideAnyone, the destroyed contract's entire balance must be paid to the owner (the caller); the mutant pays the zero address instead, so the owner's balance never increases.

For every caller other than the owner, calling sudicideAnyone must not destroy the contract (its runtime code survives); the mutant removed the owner check, so a non-owner caller self-destructs it and the code becomes empty.

For any caller other than the deployer/owner, sudicideAnyone must revert (owner-gated); the mutant removed the require so such a call succeeds (and self-destructs), making ok==false fail on M while holding for all non-owner inputs on P.

For every caller, sudicideAnyone either reverts or is called by the owner: in the reference C any non-owner call reverts, while the mutant lets any non-owner successfully self-destruct, violating the rule.

Calling sudicideAnyone (as owner, with any positive balance) always destroys C and empties its balance to the caller; the mutant self-destructs to itself so the balance never leaves, breaking address(c).balance == 0 for any positive fuzzed amount.

For any caller and any balance held by C, invoking sudicideAnyone must transfer the contract's entire balance to the caller (caller's balance grows by exactly that amount); the mutant selfdestructs to itself, so the caller's balance never increases.

For any caller (the owner) and any positive balance, invoking sudicideAnyone must transfer the contract's entire balance out so that address(c).balance becomes 0; the mutant selfdestructs to itself, leaving the full balance on the (now empty) contract address.
